responses.0: Able to groom self unaided, with or without the use of assistive devices or adapted methods
responses.1: Grooming utensils must be placed within reach before able to complete grooming activities
responses.2: Someone must assist the patient to groom self
responses.3: Patient depends entirely upon someone else for grooming needs

name: Current Ability to Dress Upper Body

responses.0: Able to get clothes out of closets and drawers, put them on and remove them from the upper body without assistance
responses.1: Able to dress upper body without assistance if clothing is laid out or handed to the patient
responses.2: Someone must help the patient put on upper body clothing
responses.3: Patient depends entirely upon another person to dress the upper body

name: Current Ability to Dress Lower Body

responses.0: Able to obtain, put on, and remove clothing and shoes without assistance
responses.1: Able to dress lower body without assistance if clothing and shoes are laid out or handed to the patient
responses.2: Someone must help the patient put on undergarments, slacks, socks or nylons, and shoes
responses.3: Patient depends entirely upon another person to dress lower body

responses.0: Able to bathe self in shower or tub independently, including getting in and out of tub/shower
responses.1: With the use of devices, is able to bathe self in shower or tub independently, including getting in and out of the tub/shower
responses.2: Able to bathe in shower or tub with the intermittent assistance of another person (supervision/reminders, getting in and out of the shower or tub, or washing difficult to reach areas)
responses.3: Able to participate in bathing self in shower or tub, but requires presence of another person throughout the bath for assistance or supervision
responses.4: Unable to use the shower or tub, but able to bathe self independently with or without the use of devices at the sink, in chair, or on commode
responses.5: Unable to use the shower or tub, but able to participate in bathing self in bed, at the sink, in bedside chair, or on commode, with the assistance or supervision of another person
responses.6: Unable to participate effectively in bathing and is bathed totally by another person

responses.0: Able to get to and from the toilet and transfer independently with or without a device
responses.1: When reminded, assisted, or supervised by another person, able to get to and from the toilet and transfer
responses.2: Unable to get to and from the toilet but is able to use a bedside commode (with or without assistance)
responses.3: Unable to get to and from the toilet or bedside commode but is able to use a bedpan/urinal independently

responses.1: Able to transfer with minimal human assistance or with use of an assistive device
responses.2: Able to bear weight and pivot during the transfer process but unable to transfer self
responses.3: Unable to transfer self and is unable to bear weight or pivot when transferred by another person
responses.4: Bedfast, unable to transfer but is able to turn and position self in bed
responses.5: Bedfast, unable to transfer and is unable to turn and position self

responses.0: Able to independently walk on even and uneven surfaces and negotiate stairs with or without railings (no human assistance or assistive device)
responses.1: With the use of a one-handed device (for example, cane, single crutch, hemi-walker), able to independently walk on even and uneven surfaces and negotiate stairs with or without railings
responses.2: Requires use of a two-handed device (for example, walker or crutches) to walk alone on a level surface and/or requires human supervision or assistance to negotiate stairs or steps or uneven surfaces
responses.3: Able to walk only with the supervision or assistance of another person at all times
responses.4: Chairfast, unable to ambulate but is able to wheel self independently
responses.5: Chairfast, unable to ambulate and is unable to wheel self
responses.6: Bedfast, unable to ambulate or be up in a chair

name: Risk of Hospitalization (check all that apply)

responses.1: History of falls (2 or more falls - or any fall with an injury - in the past 12 months)
responses.2: Unintentional weight loss of a total of 10 pounds or more in the past 12 months
responses.3: Multiple hospitalizations (2 or more) in the past 6 months
responses.4: Multiple emergency department visits (2 or more) in the past 6 months
responses.5: Decline in mental, emotional, or behavioral status in the past 3 months
responses.6: Reported or observed history of difficulty complying with any medical instructions (for example, medications, diet, exercise) in the past 3 months

name: When is the patient dyspneic or noticeably Short of Breath?

responses.0: Patient is not short of breath
responses.1: When walking more than 20 feet, climbing stairs
responses.2: With moderate exertion (for example, while dressing, using commode or bedpan, walking distances less than 20 feet)
responses.3: With minimal exertion (for example, while eating, talking, or performing other ADLs) or with agitation

responses.0: Does not apply - I have not had any pain or hurting in the past 5 days
Able to independently take the correct oral medication(s) and proper dosage(s) at the correct times
responses.1: Able to take medication(s) at the correct times if individual dosages are prepared in advance by another person, OR another person develops a drug diary or chart
responses.2: Able to take medication(s) at the correct times if given reminders by another person at the appropriate times
responses.3: Unable to take medication unless administered by another person
